summary: Fresh FOC Heat research for the Sep. 14, 2026 FOC window. One current BUY is justified: G.I. Joe: A Real American Hero/Tomb Raider #1 Cover A at $4.99 or less, limited to one copy. The key evidence is the strong aftermarket response to Lara Croft's first appearance in G.I. Joe #330, including distributor sellout and repeated completed sales for the 1:10 Lara Croft variant. The crossover #1 itself has no completed sales yet and carries a large variant program, so conviction remains moderate rather than high. Thundercats (2026) #1, Arrivals #1, and Jonah Hex and the Shadow of Death #1 are WATCH rather than BUY because supply/demand evidence is insufficient.
orderingWindow: FOC is Monday, Sep. 14, 2026. Current PRH/Comic Previews listings show Sep. 14 FOC. M&M Comics states weekly FOC orders are due 7pm Central every Monday, equivalent to 8pm Eastern in Indiana; retailer-specific deadlines can be earlier. Order earlier rather than relying on the final hour.

books.title: G.I. JOE: A REAL AMERICAN HERO/TOMB RAIDER #1
books.creators: Kyle Higgins (writer), Elena Casagrande (artist), Alex Guimarães (colorist), Pat Brosseau (letterer)
verifiedFacts: Five-issue miniseries; standard Cover A $4.99; Oct. 7, 2026 release.
First-ever G.I. JOE/Tomb Raider crossover; Lara Croft's first appearance in the shared comic continuity occurred in G.I. JOE: A Real American Hero #330.
Issue #1 has open-order standard covers plus 1:25, 1:50 and 1:100 incentives, a $5.99 foil and other variants.
marketEvidence: G.I. JOE: A Real American Hero #330 completely sold out at the distributor level after Lara Croft's surprise first appearance and was rushed back to print.
Completed-sale evidence for the #330 1:10 Steve Beach Lara Croft variant shows repeated sales generally around $20-$45, with some higher and lower outliers.
MyComicShop currently lists #330 second-print Lara Croft copies around $16-$25, confirming ongoing aftermarket attention.

Tomb Raider #1 examples from 2014 and 2016 show that Lara Croft comics can retain a collector market, but standard copies are inconsistent and therefore are not proof of a premium for this new crossover.
books.thesis: This is the clearest demand signal in the current window because the exact crossover premise already generated measurable collector demand before #1. However, the first appearance is #330, not this issue, and the high variant count raises supply risk. Buy one standard Cover A at $4.99 or less; do not chase ratios.
unknowns: Whether #1 itself becomes a durable key
Post-release completed sales for standard Cover A
Whether demand persists after the #330 novelty fades

books.title: THUNDERCATS (2026) #1
books.creators: Greg Pak (writer), David Cousens (artist); Mark Spears Cover A
verifiedFacts: New #1 relaunch; $4.99; Oct. 7, 2026 release; Sep. 14 FOC.
Fifteen covers are listed, including multiple ratios and premium/limited editions.
Story premise moves ThunderCats into a new status quo involving SilverHawks and the Mu'tants, with Lion-O becoming the Feral King.
marketEvidence: The 2024 Thundercats #1 has substantial completed-sale activity, but standard-copy sales in 2026 include $2, $3.99, $4.99 and $10-$12 examples; premium results are concentrated in variants/graded copies.
The prior series demonstrates that franchise interest can coexist with inexpensive standard copies.
Current launch coverage emphasizes the large variant program, which is supply risk rather than proof of scarcity.
books.thesis: The franchise is commercially proven and a new #1 can create attention, but the market evidence does not justify buying standard copies ahead of release. WATCH at $4.99 or below only; no ratios.

books.title: ARRIVALS #1
books.creators: Jonathan Hickman (story), Mike Del Mundo (art), Mike Huddleston (Cover A), with contributions from Nick Spencer, Christian Ward, James Stokoe, Juni Ba and others
verifiedFacts: Three-issue series presented in an oversized, prestige magazine format.
New science-fiction universe centered on the disappearance of astronaut Tajo Vallar and his children's reunion across multiple worlds.
marketEvidence: The creator package is unusually strong, but current pre-release guide values are low and are not treated as completed-sale evidence.

The closest Hickman creator comparables do not show a reliable standard-copy premium: recent completed sales for The Manhattan Projects #1 include approximately $5-$7 raw copies, with some higher-condition outliers.
The $6.99 acquisition cost is materially higher than the project's preferred entry for speculative new IP.
books.thesis: Excellent creative pedigree, weak investment evidence. The price and lack of issue-specific demand make BUY unjustified. WATCH only at $5.99 or less.

books.title: JONAH HEX AND THE SHADOW OF DEATH #1
verifiedFacts: Six-issue series; $3.99; Oct. 7, 2026 release; Sep. 14 FOC.
Horror-western interpretation of Jonah Hex, with Walsh bringing his creator-owned horror background to a DC character.
Walsh is known for The Silver Coin and Exquisite Corpses.
marketEvidence: Recent coverage is strongly creator-focused, but no reliable issue-specific completed-sale evidence exists before release.
The Silver Coin and Exquisite Corpses provide creator-demand context, not proof that this licensed DC launch will appreciate.
The lower $3.99 cover price improves downside protection relative to $6-$7 speculative launches.
books.thesis: Potentially the most interesting creator-driven WATCH after G.I. Joe, but the investment case remains unproven. One copy could be justified opportunistically at $3.99 or less, but it is not on the required shopping list.
unknowns: Collector demand for Walsh's Jonah Hex
